final.executive_summary: AAPL at $309.35 is a trim, not an exit: cut the position to a 2.0% total target of account equity (~$1,998, ~6.46 shares), selling ~3.17 shares (~$980, ~$1.00 in 10-bps fees) at the next session open. The higher alternative of 5.0% (~$4,994) requires the bull's un-fired trigger — a daily close above $314.34 on above-average volume with MACD crossing above its signal — and the lower alternative of 0.0% requires a high-volume close below $305.59, which has not printed; 2% is the exposure that respects a damaged short-term tape without betting against an intact rising 200-day SMA at $281.50, and its practical purpose is economic participation in the $310.69–329.59 gap-fill and the late-October FQ4 catalyst at a size where an adverse 9% move to the 200 SMA costs ~$175, or ~0.18% of total equity. I am accepting the cash opportunity cost deliberately: ~97% of the account earns no interest and forfeits the gap reclaim, but cash is the option to re-enter on the bull's own confirmed trigger rather than on hope. Narrative conditions only, no implemented orders: restore toward 4–5% on a close above $314.34 with above-average volume and MACD > signal; cut to 0% on a close below $305.59 (references $289.82, then $281.50); do not re-add inside the $309–311 collision zone on weak volume.
final.investment_thesis: The risk debate converged on the direction and split only on degree, and the degree question resolves against the aggressive analyst. All three seats agree AAPL's short-term structure is impaired: price sits below the 10 EMA ($310.35), the 50 SMA ($310.21) and the Bollinger midline ($314.34), MACD at −1.574 is below its −1.194 signal, the 8/20 push to $320.28 was rejected and closed at $311.30, and the $310.69–329.59 gap void sits directly overhead having been created on ~2.5x average volume. Where the aggressive analyst breaks down is his claim that 'cutting also requires a 305.59 confirmation.' The conservative analyst answers this correctly: risk management does not require first losing to the invalidation level before de-risking, and carrying 2.98% passively through a negative-momentum, 2.5x-volume distribution structure is pre-event risk-taking, not patience. The neutral analyst is right that the 2% versus 2.98% argument is noise-level in trend terms but is not noise in risk terms — it is the difference between an exposure justified by today's total-target assessment and one inherited from yesterday's holding, which the sizing rules explicitly forbid anchoring to. The bear's accounting points survive scrutiny and temper the bull's headline: sequential operating margin compressed from 34.02% (H1) to 32.62% (Q3) even as gross margin peaked at 50.06%, and roughly $10.8B of the $35.2B OCF increase looks like a cash-tax timing benefit (cash taxes −28.9% versus book tax +40.7%) that the source itself flags as unexplained. The bull still wins the franchise question decisively enough to forbid liquidation: nine-month revenue +16.1%, record Q3 gross margin 50.06% (+357bp), FCF +52.5% to $110.2B, net cash nearly doubled to $62.2B, debt/equity 0.78x with no new long-term issuance, R&D +32.5% funded by gross-margin expansion rather than decay, and price 9.9% above a 200-day SMA that has risen every session in the sample (268.49 -> 281.50) with the 50 SMA 28.71 points above it. Decline volume at ~0.88x average shows selling drying up rather than accelerating, and the $300–302 shelf has held three weeks. Sizing logic, stated explicitly against both boundaries: 5.0% (~$4,994, ~16.1 shares) is the allocation I would authorize on the bull's confirmed trigger — a close above $314.34 on above-average volume with MACD > signal — because that opens 316.8 -> 320.3 -> 329.6, but it is not in hand and the 8/20 breakout already failed; 0.0% would be defensible only on a close below $305.59 on above-average volume, which would open $289.82 and then $281.50, but the primary trend is unbroken and the fundamental record is not deteriorating, so full liquidation would discard a rising 200 SMA, a dataset-high gross margin and a mechanically identifiable +6.5% gap-fill objective. Between those boundaries, 2.0% keeps us economically long the gap-fill and the late-October Q4 catalyst — the residual is a real allocation, not an 'observation' placeholder, and it clears the ~$1.00 transaction cost. The cash opportunity cost is the honest cost of this call: with cash at ~97% of the account and earning nothing, a reclaim of $314.34 and gap-fill to $329.59 is forfeited, and I accept that because the near-term evidence (failed breakout, price under every short and medium average, MACD below signal, 6.1% distribution gap overhead, invalidation 1.2% away) makes the next several weeks a coin flip at best. What would change it: an upgrade toward Overweight on a daily close above $314.34 with above-average volume and MACD > signal, confirmed above $318.43, and a Q4 print with gross margin >=49.5% with inventory flat-to-down; a downgrade to Sell on a high-volume close below $305.59, on Q4 gross margin below 48%, or if the unexplained ~$13B intangible build against ~$13.5B of new noncurrent liabilities proves to carry amortization or impairment risk. Stated gaps, not papered over: the news sample covers roughly 20 of 90 eligible records with blanks around 8/14–8/18, so the Q4-deceleration narrative cannot be verified; there is no Q4 guidance or consensus, no options or positioning data, no insider data (explicitly unavailable — neither side leaned on it), and no live quote beyond the 2026-08-21 close of $309.35. Prior AAPL lessons bind: the 2026-08-13 Underweight (+3.9% alpha) and 2026-08-12 Underweight (+5.3% alpha) were directionally wrong and taught that trimming on momentum decay inside a rising primary trend is expensive, which is why the reduction stops at 2% and not 0%; the 2026-08-14 Overweight reflection warned that gated scaling left size undeployed into a call already decided on fundamentals, which is why this is a single explicit total target rather than a staged sequence; and the 2026-07-30/07-31 Underweights earned their alpha only when anchored to a real distribution print, which the 07-31 gap on 132.5M shares provides here.
